data.title: Brookfield Renewable Partners Amends Proposed Simplification Ahead of December Vote
data.description:
Brookfield Renewable Partners ( ($TSE:BEP.UN) ) just unveiled an announcement.

Brookfield Renewable Partners L.P. announced on November 27, 2026, amendments to its proposed corporate-structure simplification involving Brookfield Renewable Corporation and Brookfield Renewable Partners Inc. The change followed more than 99% of votes cast supporting the proposal, while those votes represented about 62% of outstanding BEP units—insufficient for the originally contemplated two-thirds approval of a limited partnership agreement amendment.

Under the amended plan, BEP units would be exchanged one-for-one for BEP Inc. Class A shares, while BEP would become a BEP Inc. subsidiary; the transaction remains subject to Unitholder approval at a December 9, 2026 meeting requiring at least two-thirds of votes cast. If approved, BEP units would be delisted, BEP Inc. Class A shares would be listed subject to TSX and NYSE approval, and BEPC would be delisted and cease to be a reporting issuer.

data.title: Infobird Agrees to Sell Up to $10 Million in Convertible Notes
data.description:
Infobird Co ( (IFBD) ) has issued an announcement.

On November 26, 2026, Infobird Co., Ltd. entered into an agreement with a non-U.S. investor to sell convertible promissory notes with aggregate principal of up to $10 million in one or more closings through December 31, 2027. The notes carry 10% simple annual interest, mature 24 months after issuance and rank equally with the company’s other unsecured, unsubordinated obligations.

The investor may convert the notes into ordinary shares at 50% of the lowest closing price during the preceding five trading days, subject to a $0.50 floor and Nasdaq issuance limits absent shareholder approval. The agreement also provides for possible prepayment at 115%, default remedies and investor-demanded resale registration. The notes and shares were offered to a non-U.S. person under Regulation S and were not registered under U.S. securities laws.

data.title: Gulf Resources Agrees to Acquire Bromine and Salt Assets
data.description:
Gulf Resources ( (GURE) ) just unveiled an update.

On November 24, 2026, Gulf Resources and its wholly owned subsidiary, Shouguang City Haoyuan Chemical Company Limited, agreed to acquire bromine and crude salt production assets from the collective economic organization of Caiyangzi Village in Shouguang City, China. The assets include facilities, equipment and approximately 1.29 square kilometers of crude salt fields.

The purchase price was RMB 103,547,899, comprising RMB 95,247,999 in cash and 355,000 restricted Gulf Resources shares valued at RMB 8,299,900. Closing was scheduled by December 31, 2026, subject to a satisfactory asset assessment and other conditions, including signed documents from the stock recipients.

data.title: ZenaTech Secures C$270,000 in Energy-Sector Survey Contracts
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from ZenaTech, Inc. ( (ZENA) ).

ZenaTech is a technology company specializing in AI drone platforms, Drone as a Service (DaaS), enterprise SaaS and quantum computing solutions. On November 17, 2026, it said its DaaS business secured survey contracts with two established energy-sector customers, including C$270,000 under contract for plant construction, infrastructure development and plant-site inspection.

The customers were an established Canadian oil and gas producer and a major energy infrastructure company. ZenaTech’s network combines licensed surveying with drone mapping and centralized LiDAR processing, while the company currently operates almost 45 DaaS locations across the U.S., Canada, U.K., Ireland, UAE and Australia.

data.title: Propanc Biopharma Announces Convertible Note Financing and Warrants
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from Propanc Biopharma ( (PPCB) ).

On November 20, 2026, Propanc Biopharma entered separate agreements with Eleven 11 Management and Hexstone Capital to issue and sell convertible notes with aggregate principal of $3 million and warrants for a $2.1 million subscription. At the initial closing, the company issued notes totaling $2.22 million and warrants to purchase up to 1,268,573 common shares; the broader transaction included $2 million in cash consideration from Eleven 11 and credits for Hexstone.

The initial notes were issued at a 30% original issue discount, bear 14% annual interest, mature on August 20, 2027, and are convertible at the holders’ election at $1.75 per share, subject to adjustments and ownership and Nasdaq limits. The warrants have $1.75 exercise prices, are immediately exercisable and expire on their fourth anniversary, while the securities were sold without registration under applicable Securities Act exemptions.

data.title: Maison Solutions Receives Nasdaq Deficiency Notice After Board Resignation
data.description:
Maison Solutions Inc. Class A ( (MSS) ) has shared an announcement.

Maison Solutions announced on November 27, 2026, that Nasdaq had issued a notice of deficiency on November 24 after Bin Wang’s resignation from the Board and Audit Committee became effective on November 20, leaving the committee with two members rather than the three independent members required under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5605(c)(2)(A).

The company had notified Nasdaq of the deficiency on November 19, and Nasdaq’s notice stated that the company would have a cure period ending at the earlier of its next annual shareholders’ meeting or November 20, 2027, or, if that meeting occurs before May 19, 2027, no later than May 19, 2027. Maison said it was searching for an additional independent director and expected to fill the vacancy within the cure period.

data.title: Rocky Mountain Chocolate Factory Faces Nasdaq Listing Compliance Review
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from Rocky Mountain Chocolate Factory ( (RMCF) ).

On November 24, 2026, Nasdaq notified Rocky Mountain Chocolate Factory that its common stock had closed below the $1 minimum bid price for 30 consecutive business days, creating a 180-calendar-day compliance period through May 24, 2027. The notice had no immediate effect on listing or trading; compliance required a closing bid price of at least $1 for 10 consecutive business days, while a further compliance period and potential delisting were conditional.

Also on November 24, 2026, the company amended Interim Chief Executive Officer Allen C. Harper’s offer letter, extending his original six-month service term by an additional six months while continuing his annual base salary of $140,000. Harper received a $130,000 RSU grant calculated using the 20-day volume-weighted average stock price before the grant date, with vesting in six equal monthly installments beginning January 8, 2027, subject to continued service as interim CEO.

data.title: Malibu Boats Reaches SEC Settlement Over Disclosure Issues
data.description:
Malibu Boats ( (MBUU) ) has provided an update.

Malibu Boats, Inc. reached an agreement in principle with the SEC under which it would pay a $300,000 civil penalty to settle an investigation into statements about channel inventory levels and its relationship with Tommy’s Boats during fiscal years 2023 and 2024.

The contemplated resolution addressed alleged negligent misstatements in reports covering the third quarter of fiscal 2023 through the first quarter of fiscal 2024 and an alleged failure to disclose the deteriorating relationship from December 2023 and/or January 2024 until April 2024; the company said it did not believe the resolution would materially affect its financial position.

data.title: Sol-Gel Technologies Announces Nov. 30 Call on SGT-610 Top-Line Results
data.description:

Sol-Gel Technologies is a specialized dermatology company advancing therapies for rare and serious skin diseases. Its products and candidates include FDA-approved TWYNEO and EPSOLAY, plus investigational SGT-610 and SGT-210; SGT-610 is being developed to prevent new basal cell carcinoma lesions in adults with Gorlin syndrome.

On November 27, 2026, Sol-Gel announced it would host a conference call on November 30 to discuss top-line results from pivotal Phase 3 trial SGT-610-01. The trial was evaluating SGT-610, patidegib gel 2%, for preventing basal cell carcinoma lesions in adults with Gorlin syndrome.

data.title: Grown Rogue Announces New York Cannabis Acquisition Agreement
data.description:
Grown Rogue International ( (TSE:GRIN) ) has shared an update.

On November 23, 2026, Grown Rogue New York, LLC, a 51%-owned subsidiary, signed membership-interest and asset purchase agreements with PharmaCann and related parties to acquire 100% of PharmaCann of New York’s membership interests and other business assets, including its New York cannabis licenses, Hamptonburgh cultivation and processing facility, and four dispensaries. Completion remained subject to Office of Cannabis Management approval and other closing conditions.

Closing required OCM approval of GRNY as a true party in interest and transfer of license control, simultaneous completion of both agreements, treatment of unpaid taxes, lien releases and no material adverse effect on PCNY. The purchase price was $1.8 million in cash, reduced from $3.1 million for PharmaCann’s 50% share of an approximately $2.4 million New York adult-use cannabis tax assessment and $0.1 million of equipment lease reimbursements. Under an August 20, 2026 agreement, GRNY agreed to provide operational, general and administrative consulting and a secured working-capital line of credit of up to $9.0 million; by November 23, it had begun supporting the operating transition, including cultivation restart at Hamptonburgh.

data.title: AI Financial Announces CFO Transition and Fiscal Year Change
data.description:
The latest update is out from AI Financial Corporation ( (AIFC) ).

Effective November 23, 2026, Steven Plumb transitioned out of AI Financial Corporation’s chief financial officer role and into the same role at Drew Therapeutics Corporation, the company’s biotechnology subsidiary. Tony Isaac, AI Financial’s chief executive officer and a director, assumed the acting chief financial officer role without a change in compensation.

The company changed its fiscal year from a 52/53-week year to a calendar year, moving the 2026 year-end from December 26 to December 31 and setting subsequent year-ends for December 31. The board approved the change on November 23, 2026, in accordance with the company’s bylaws.

data.title: Opendoor Technologies Announces $300 Million At-the-Market Offering
data.description:
An update from Opendoor Technologies ( (OPEN) ) is now available.

On November 27, 2026, Opendoor Technologies entered a Sales Agreement with Virtu Americas LLC as sales agent and/or principal, allowing the company to offer and sell, at its discretion, up to $300 million of common stock. The agreement permits sales through an at-the-market offering, with Virtu eligible to receive commissions of up to 2.0% of gross sales prices.

The company established the offering to complement existing capital resources and provide flexibility to access equity markets opportunistically when market conditions are attractive and sales are viewed as being in stockholders’ long-term interests. Opendoor is not required to sell shares, and the timing and amount of any sales will depend on market conditions and other factors.
